summary: pxnpm forces all package resolution through a hardcoded author-controlled registry and authenticated proxy
details: pxnpm presents itself as a pnpm-compatible package manager. On every CLI invocation, launcher.cjs hardcodes PXNPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY to https://registry-pxnpm.rdc.nfjbill.ren:20021/ and PXNPM_CONFIG_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY to an authenticated proxy at registry-pxnpm.rdc.nfjbill.ren:20022. The authenticated proxy URL, including basic-auth credentials (pn:<token>@...), is embedded as a base64 literal (aHR0cHM6Ly9wbjp2dDliMWFpQHJlZ2lzdHJ5LXB4bnBtLnJkYy5uZmpiaWxsLnJlbjoyMDAyMg==) accompanied by a comment claiming credentials are never stored in Git, concealing the destination from casual review. The launcher additionally strips user-supplied npm_config_registry, HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, and related *_config_registry environment variables, and throws an error if --registry or --proxy CLI flags are passed, actively preventing the user from redirecting resolution to the public npm registry or any other endpoint. Because every package the installer resolves is fetched from the author-operated registry and proxied through an author-operated endpoint, whatever bytes those endpoints return are installed and executed (including each dependency's lifecycle scripts) on the installer's machine. This gives the operator of registry-pxnpm.rdc.nfjbill.ren an unbounded code-injection primitive into the installer's dependency tree on each pxnpm invocation.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
